learning_objective: The learner will apply the differences among a link, an embed, a Common Cartridge import, and an LTI tool to choose the best way to bring a resource into an LMS for each of six teacher needs, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** lms-integration-chooser
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the differences among a link, an embed, a Common Cartridge import, and an LTI tool to choose the best way to bring a resource into an LMS for each of six teacher needs, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** LMS Import, Common Cartridge, LTI Integration, Iframe Embedding, Link Sharing (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each need the learner commits one of four methods. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct method column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the method list is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) An embed copies the resource into the LMS. (2) A Common Cartridge only works inside one LMS. (3) LTI is just a fancy link. **Instructional Rationale:** Choosing a method for a need is an Apply-level action. Six needs that map to four methods teach the learner what each method does and does not give a teacher. **Content:** The four methods: Link (students open the resource at its own address), Embed (the resource appears on the course page through a frame), Common Cartridge import (a whole unit is copied into the LMS as a package), LTI tool (an external tool opens inside the LMS and can send results back). The six needs: | # | Teacher need shown to the learner | Correct method | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | "I want students to open one reading in a new tab." | Link | A link opens the resource at its own address. | | 2 | "I want a simulation to appear on my course page." | Embed | A frame shows the simulation inside the page. | | 3 | "I want to copy a whole unit, with pages, quizzes, and files, into my course." | Common Cartridge import | A package carries the whole unit into the LMS. | | 4 | "I want an external quiz tool to send each student's score to the LMS gradebook." | LTI tool | LTI lets the tool exchange information with the LMS. | | 5 | "I want colleagues in another school, with a different LMS, to receive the same unit." | Common Cartridge import | A cartridge is the common exchange form between LMSs. | | 6 | "I want students to read chapter 4 of an open textbook." | Link | A link to the chapter is enough. | **Provenance:** The needs are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The methods follow the chapter sections "LMS Import", "Common Cartridge", "LTI Integration", "Iframe Embedding", and "Link Sharing". **Rules:** Each need has exactly one correct method. Two needs call for a Link, one for an Embed, two for a Common Cartridge import, and one for an LTI tool. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one need and the four methods. 2. The learner may open the method descriptions. Opening them does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses a method, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After need 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 needs in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [method]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The best method is [method]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can choose how to bring a resource into an LMS." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed need. **Starting State:** The first need and the four methods. The question shown is "Which method fits this need?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a teacher can bring an OER into an LMS by link, embed, file upload, or package import, that a Common Cartridge is a single package that moves between LMSs, and that LTI lets an external tool exchange information with an LMS.
